source.title: Phonological Abstraction and Exception Memorization in Noisy Tone Learning
source.authors: Yi Yang; Yi-Ming Wang; Jia-Hong Yuan

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own training trajectories on noisy speech-tone learning and explicitly contrasts their abstraction-before-memorization order with grokking, which it describes as generalization following training-set fitting. This is a challenge to grokking-like delayed generalization in the tested speech setting, not a reproduction of the algorithmic task.
record.gate_note: The paper's own speech-learning trajectories are relevant to V3. Its references to the original grokking studies are background, not results from those studies. It does not test small algorithmic datasets, Fourier circuits, weight decay or weight norm, LLM training, or optimizer/numerical artifact explanations.
record.test_reason: The study tracks training on noisy-label Mandarin tone classification and finds generalization first, then memorization of corrupted labels. It mentions grokking only as a contrasting ordering in Background and Discussion. It does not test V3's claim: it never varies initialization scale, weight norm or the lazy/rich regime. It fine-tunes a pretrained model with label noise and selects checkpoints by validation loss. V3 does not predict a delay in this setting, so the absence of one neither supports nor challenges V3. No other version is touched: there are no algorithmic tasks, circuits, weight decay, LLM training or optimizer-artifact controls. The finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. In recoverable regimes, wav2vec2.0 first shows abstraction-consistent tone behaviour and later fits corrupted labels as exceptions. This order persists under encoder truncation and random initialization, and rank compression does not selectively separate abstraction from memorization. Fitted exceptions are more fragile than abstraction-consistent predictions under acoustic perturbation. The contrast with grokking is a one-sentence remark in the Discussion, not a tested conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes pretrained speech models on noisy Mandarin tone labels and tracks abstraction-consistent generalization and corrupted-label fitting; it does not use an algorithmic dataset or the original grokking setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The trajectories vary with label-noise regime and training scale. The paper reports that the abstraction-before-memorization ordering persists under random initialization; pretraining improves sample efficiency and noise robustness.

fits_no_version.finding: In fine-tuned wav2vec2.0 large, HuBERT and randomly initialized wav2vec2.0 on tone labels with uniform label noise, test accuracy and self-correction peak early (around epochs 5–7). Corrupted-label memorization rises later to about 100%. At high noise (70%), test accuracy then falls sharply rather than rising late.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On noisy-label non-algorithmic tasks, networks learn the shared structure before memorizing noise (generalization precedes memorization), the opposite of grokking's ordering.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026
record.problems: Reported numbers are single-run percentages; no error bars or uncertainty estimates are given. The study uses a speech-tone task and synthetic random label replacements, so its results do not establish behavior on the other non-algorithmic settings named in V3.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported trajectory results were left out. Endpoint scale-noise accuracies and acoustic perturbation probes were not included because they do not measure delayed generalization during training.

untested.parts: No small algorithmic datasets; no relation between delay and training-set size.
No circuit or progress-measure analysis; behaviour-level metrics only.
No initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation and no lazy/rich comparison. The speech task with label noise is not tested as a grokking setting.
No weight decay, critical dataset size or ungrokking.
No comparison of algorithms across runs.

missing.what: HuBERT epoch-wise trajectories at 10% scale across 0–90% noise, showing the same early-generalization, late-memorization order. Best-validation epochs are 4–13.

Depth-control and post-encoder rank runs: final train accuracy about 100% with last test accuracy around 50–58%, against best-validation test accuracy of 83–90%. This shows test accuracy declines after training fit, with no late rise.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5 challenges V3' overreaches. V3 is an existence and regime-dependence claim, and this study manipulates neither initialization scale nor weight norm. A grokking-free noisy-label fine-tuning run is not a setting where V3 predicts a delay. All results are single runs without uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses Mandarin tone classification with noisy speech labels, not small algorithmic datasets; it does not test the stated delayed rise in test accuracy as training-set size shrinks.

It tracks behavioral measures over training but does not identify or measure a generalizing circuit, memorizing circuit components, or whether circuit-level progress measures anticipate a test-accuracy jump.
The study tests noisy speech-tone learning, including a random-initialization control, but not images, text, molecules, initialization-scale sweeps, or weight-norm interventions.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested.
The study does not test weight decay or another low-norm bias, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
The study does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits in the softmax.

rows.subject: wav2vec2.0 large
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned from wav2vec2.0 large pretrained on 960 hours of LibriSpeech audio
rows.operation_detail: Track test accuracy across training epochs
rows.value: Changes little from the peak to the final epoch (90.1% → 88.3%); exception memorization rises later to near-perfect levels.
rows.note: The study describes abstraction-consistent test performance as appearing early and remaining stable, while corrupted-label fitting occurs later—the reverse of delayed generalization after overfitting.
rows.check: Test accuracy on fine-tuned wav2vec2.0 large under label noise, with no regime manipulation V3 names. 'Reversed' overstates it: V3 predicts no grokking in this setting.

rows.subject: wav2vec2.0 large
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned from wav2vec2.0 large pretrained on 960 hours of LibriSpeech audio
rows.operation_detail: Track exception memorization across training epochs
rows.value: Rises later to near-perfect levels, while test accuracy changes little from peak to final epoch (90.1% → 88.3%).
rows.note: The reported ordering is early abstraction-consistent generalization followed by later exception fitting.
rows.check: Measures fitting of corrupted labels (noise memorization), not delayed generalization. This is a different construct from grokking.

rows.subject: wav2vec2.0 large
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned from wav2vec2.0 large pretrained on 960 hours of LibriSpeech audio
rows.operation_detail: Track test accuracy across training epochs
rows.value: After the peak, test accuracy drops by 37.9 points by the final epoch.
rows.note: The model first reaches substantial test generalization, then loses it during continued training; it does not show a delayed test-accuracy rise.
rows.check: Test accuracy peaks early (73.4%) and then drops 37.9 points, an early-stopping/noise-overfitting pattern. It is not a test of V3's regime-switching claim.

rows.subject: wav2vec2.0 large
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned from wav2vec2.0 large pretrained on 960 hours of LibriSpeech audio
rows.value: Drops by 62.7 points by the final epoch.
rows.note: This accompanying measure declines as continued training shifts toward fitting corrupted labels.
rows.check: Self-correction on corrupted positions is the study's own probe and does not measure a grokking delay.

rows.subject: wav2vec2.0 large

rows.operation_detail: Track test accuracy across training epochs
rows.note: The paper says the abstraction-consistent phase never becomes reliable in this setting.
rows.check: Peak test accuracy of 29.8% at 90% noise is near the 5-class chance level. It shows no recoverable signal, which bears on no version.

rows.subject: randomly initialized wav2vec2.0
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; trained from the first update
rows.operation_detail: Track test accuracy across training epochs
rows.value: 51.36%, 77.78%, 64.67%, 47.09%, 48.24%, respectively; the best checkpoint is at epoch 5.
rows.note: Test accuracy peaks early and then declines rather than rising after prolonged overfitting.
rows.check: The random-initialization control uses a different learning rate (1e-4) and a fixed initialization scheme. It does not sweep initialization scale, so it is not V3's lazy-to-rich manipulation.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Noisy Mandarin tone learning with pretrained wav2vec2.0 at the reported representative settings, and the random-initialization control
reader_labels.reason: The reported trajectories show abstraction-consistent test performance appearing early or failing to become reliable, followed by later exception fitting; they do not show delayed generalization after overfitting (R1-R9).
